ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle B=\angle C$, point $D$ is on side $BC$, and point $E$ is on $AC$, $\angle ADE=\angle AED$. If $\angle BAD=40^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle CDE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle ADC$ is an exterior angle of $\triangle ABD$, \\
we have $\angle ADC=\angle BAD+\angle B=40^\circ+\angle B$, \\
Since $\angle AED$ is an exterior angle of $\triangle DEC$, \\
we have $\angle AED=\angle C+\angle EDC$, \\
Since $\angle ADE=\angle AED$, \\
we have $\angle ADE=\angle C+\angle EDC$, \\
Since $\angle ADC=\angle ADE+\angle EDC=\angle C+2\angle EDC$, \\
and since $\angle B=\angle C$, \\
we have $\angle B+40^\circ=\angle B+2\angle EDC$, \\
Therefore, $\angle EDC=\boxed{20^\circ}$.

In triangle ABD, since DB and DC are opposite rays on line BC, ∠ADC is the exterior angle at D. Therefore ∠ADC = ∠BAD + ∠B = 40° + x. In triangle DEC, since AE is the extension of CE along line AC, ∠AED is the exterior angle at E. Therefore ∠AED = ∠C + ∠CDE = x + y. Given ∠ADE = ∠AED, we get ∠ADE = x + y. From the diagram, ray DE lies inside ∠ADC, so ∠ADC = ∠ADE + ∠CDE = (x + y) + y = x + 2y. Equating the two expressions for ∠ADC gives x + 40° = x + 2y, so 2y = 40° and y = 20°. Final answer: ∠CDE = 20°.
